2.5.1.6-f16.accuracy_reason: Antonio Luiz (Antonius Ludovicus) was a Lisbon physician who wrote De pudore (1540). Olisipo/Olysippo is the Latin name for Lisbon.

2.5.1.6-f18.accuracy_reason: Lac virginale was a milky cosmetic wash made from litharge (lead oxide), and Burton glosses it himself as 'strained liquor of Litharge'.

2.5.1.6-f2.accuracy_reason: The officinal pilulae de cynoglosso contained opium (with henbane and other ingredients) and were given as a soporific.

2.5.1.6-f24.accuracy_reason: Requies Nicolai was an opiate electuary from the Nicolaus antidotary, and the note hedges the attribution. Burton does later quote Rulandus calling it 'ultimum refugium'.

2.5.1.6-f25.accuracy_reason: Triphera magna was a standard opiate electuary of the Nicolaus antidotary and the later pharmacopoeias.

2.5.1.6-f42.accuracy_reason: Diascordium, Fracastoro's electuary, contained scordium (water germander) and opium.

2.5.1.6-f6.accuracy_reason: Unguentum populeum was made from poplar buds together with narcotic leaves such as poppy, henbane, mandrake and nightshade, and was used as a cooling soporific.
